Luís de Camões, The Lusiads, translated by Richard F. Burton.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/luis-de-camoes/the-lusiads/richard-f-burton

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Luís de Camões, the author, died 1580.
- Richard F. Burton, the translator, died 1890.

First publication of the text used: 1880 (SE colophon: 'It was translated from Portuguese in 1880 by Richard F. Burton.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1880, before 1931; a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 1975.
- Country of origin (the facts do not name the country of first publication): the last person to die did so in 1890. The text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, from 1 January 1991.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'The Lusiads was published in 1572 by Luís de Camões. It was translated from Portuguese in 1880 by Richard F. Burton.'
